title: Wang Mang interrupts Han rule
summary: Wang Mang takes the imperial title and establishes the Xin dynasty. His ambitious land and currency reforms face resistance amid natural disasters and rebellions; Han rule is later restored.
significance: The short interregnum exposes tensions over landholding, reform and imperial legitimacy in early China.

zh.title: 王莽代汉建立新朝
zh.summary: 王莽称帝建立新朝。他推行土地与货币改革，但在自然灾害和起义中遭遇阻力；汉朝统治后来恢复。
zh.significance: 这一短暂插曲揭示了早期中国土地占有、改革与皇权合法性之间的矛盾。

title: Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish preacher from Galilee who teaches about the coming kingdom of God, is arrested in Jerusalem and executed by crucifixion on the orders of the Roman governor Pontius Pilate. His followers soon proclaim that he has risen from the dead. Most historians accept that he existed and was crucified, but the exact year is uncertain, with AD 30 and 33 the most often proposed.
significance: His followers' belief in his resurrection became the center of Christianity, which spread across the Roman world and is today the world's largest religion.

zh.title: 耶稣被钉十字架
zh.summary: 罗马总督本丢·彼拉多治下，耶稣在耶路撒冷被钉十字架，通常定于公元30年或33年。基督徒相信他死后复活。
zh.significance: 他的死亡与复活信仰成为基督教核心，也使十字架成为世界最广为识别的宗教象征之一。

title: Kushan Empire
summary: The Kushans, descended from the Yuezhi nomads, built an empire reaching from Central Asia across Afghanistan into northern India. Under kings such as Kanishka they controlled the trade routes between Rome, Persia, India and China and patronized Buddhism.
significance: Through the Kushan realm Buddhism and its Greek-influenced Gandharan art travelled along the Silk Road into Central Asia and China.

zh.title: 贵霜帝国
zh.summary: 贵霜统治者出自迁入中亚的月氏人，建立横跨今阿富汗、巴基斯坦与北印度的帝国，连接印度洋贸易与丝绸之路，支持佛教及多种宗教传统。
zh.significance: 贵霜促进希腊、伊朗与印度文化交融，并帮助佛教经中亚传播到中国。

title: Roman conquest of Britain
summary: Emperor Claudius sends an army of some 40,000 men across the Channel, probably landing at Richborough in Kent, and takes the British tribal center of Camulodunum (Colchester). Conquest of the rest of the island is slow and contested, including the revolt of Queen Boudica around AD 60, and Rome never permanently holds the far north of Scotland.
significance: Britain remained a Roman province for nearly four centuries, gaining towns such as London, roads and Hadrian's Wall before Roman rule ended in the early 400s.

zh.title: 罗马征服不列颠
zh.summary: 克劳狄皇帝派约四万军队渡海，可能在肯特里奇伯勒登陆，并攻占卡穆洛杜努姆，即今科尔切斯特。征服过程漫长，约公元60年发生布狄卡起义。罗马从未长期控制苏格兰最北部。
zh.significance: 不列颠大部分地区作为罗马行省近四百年，修建了伦敦等城镇、道路与哈德良长城，直到5世纪初罗马统治结束。
zh.locationName: 里奇伯勒（可能的登陆点）

title: Funan
summary: Funan, the Chinese name for a kingdom in the lower Mekong, grew rich on sea trade between India and China. Finds at its port of Oc Eo include Roman coins and Indian jewelry, and its rulers adopted Indian ideas of kingship, religion and writing.
significance: It is the earliest known state in Southeast Asia and an early channel by which Indian culture reached the region.

zh.title: 扶南
zh.summary: 扶南是湄公河下游王国的中文名称，依靠印度与中国之间的海上贸易致富。俄厄港发现罗马钱币和印度饰物，其统治者接受印度的王权、宗教与文字观念。
zh.significance: 扶南是东南亚最早可知的国家之一，也是印度文化传入该地区的重要渠道。

title: A merchant guide to the Indian Ocean
summary: An anonymous Greek-speaking writer describes ports, commodities and sailing routes from the Red Sea to India. The Periplus is usually dated to the middle of the first century AD.
significance: It provides unusually detailed evidence of commercial links between Africa, Arabia, India and the Roman world.

zh.title: 印度洋商人航海指南
zh.summary: 一位匿名希腊语作者记述从红海到印度的港口、商品与航线。《厄立特里亚海航行记》通常定于公元1世纪中叶。
zh.significance: 它为非洲、阿拉伯、印度与罗马世界的商业联系提供了罕见的详细证据。

title: Buddhism reaches China
summary: According to tradition, Emperor Ming of the Han dynasty dreams of a golden figure, sends envoys west, and in AD 68 founds the White Horse Temple at Luoyang for two Indian monks who arrive with Buddhist scriptures. The story is legendary in its details; Buddhism probably reached China gradually with merchants and missionaries along the Silk Road, and a Han prince is already recorded supporting Buddhist monks a few years earlier.
significance: Buddhism became one of China's major religions, and from China it spread to Korea, Japan and Vietnam.

zh.title: 佛教传入中国
zh.summary: 相传汉明帝梦见金人，遣使西行，并于公元68年在洛阳建立白马寺，安置携经而来的两位印度僧人。故事细节带有传说色彩；佛教更可能随商人与传教者沿丝绸之路逐步传入，且此前数年已有汉朝宗室支持僧人的记载。
zh.significance: 佛教成为中国主要宗教之一，又从中国传播到朝鲜、日本和越南。

title: Destruction of the Second Temple
summary: During a great Jewish revolt against Roman rule, a Roman army under Titus, son of the emperor Vespasian, besieges Jerusalem for months, then storms the city and burns the Temple. Much of the city is destroyed, and many of its people are killed or enslaved.
significance: Without the Temple and its sacrifices, Judaism re-centered on synagogues, prayer and the study of scripture led by rabbis, while the Arch of Titus in Rome still shows the Temple's treasures carried off in triumph.

zh.title: 第二圣殿被毁
zh.summary: 罗马军队在提图斯率领下镇压犹太起义，攻陷耶路撒冷并摧毁第二圣殿，造成大量死亡与流散。
zh.significance: 圣殿祭祀中心消失，犹太教逐渐以经学、律法与会堂生活为核心，事件也成为犹太历史记忆的重要转折。

title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
summary: Mount Vesuvius, near the Bay of Naples, erupts violently and buries the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash, pumice and searing flows of hot gas and rock. Thousands die. The traditional date is 24 August, but some evidence suggests the eruption came a few weeks later, in October.
significance: Rediscovered from the 1700s, the buried towns preserve houses, paintings, shops and graffiti that give an unusually detailed picture of everyday Roman life.

zh.title: 维苏威火山掩埋庞贝
zh.summary: 维苏威火山猛烈喷发，以火山灰和炽热物质掩埋庞贝、赫库兰尼姆及附近聚落，造成大量居民死亡。
zh.significance: 遗址保存建筑、壁画、器物乃至生活痕迹，为了解罗马日常生活提供独特窗口。

title: Kingdom of Aksum
summary: From its capital in the Ethiopian highlands and its Red Sea port of Adulis, Aksum traded ivory and gold with Rome, Arabia and India. Its kings minted their own coins, raised giant stone stelae and in the 4th century adopted Christianity.
significance: Aksum was one of the great trading powers of late antiquity and the origin of Ethiopian Christianity and the Ge'ez literary tradition.

zh.title: 阿克苏姆王国
zh.summary: 阿克苏姆在今埃塞俄比亚、厄立特里亚高地兴起，通过红海港口参与罗马、阿拉伯与印度之间的贸易，铸造钱币并树立巨大石碑，后来接受基督教。
zh.significance: 它是古代非洲重要强国，也是埃塞俄比亚与厄立特里亚基督教传统的源头。

title: Ban Zhao writes Lessons for Women
summary: Ban Zhao sets out advice on women's conduct and learning in a work generally dated to the early second century. It advocates education while accepting a strongly hierarchical gender order.
significance: The work shaped later prescriptions for women and provides evidence of both female scholarship and its social constraints.

zh.title: 班昭撰写《女诫》
zh.summary: 班昭在通常定于2世纪初的著作中讨论女性行为与学习，倡导女性受教育，同时接受强烈的性别等级秩序。
zh.significance: 著作影响了后世女性行为规范，也反映了女性学术活动及其社会限制。

title: Kingdom of Funan
summary: In the lower Mekong region of what is now southern Vietnam and Cambodia, the kingdom known by its Chinese name, Funan, grows rich on sea trade between India and China. At its port of Oc Eo, archaeologists have found Roman coins, Indian beads and Chinese goods. Much of what is known about Funan comes from Chinese records, and its beginnings are uncertain.
significance: Funan is often seen as one of the earliest states of Southeast Asia, and it helped bring Indian ideas about kingship, religion and writing into the region.

zh.title: 扶南王国
zh.summary: 湄公河下游今越南南部、柬埔寨一带的扶南王国，凭借印度与中国之间的海上贸易兴起。俄厄港出土罗马钱币、印度珠饰及中国商品。有关扶南的知识多来自中国记载，其起源年代尚不明确。
zh.significance: 扶南常被视为东南亚最早的国家之一，推动了印度王权、宗教与文字观念的传播。
zh.locationName: 湄公河三角洲俄厄（扶南港口）

title: Moche culture
summary: In the river valleys of Peru's dry north coast, the Moche built irrigation canals and huge adobe pyramids such as the Huaca del Sol. Their potters and metalworkers produced lifelike portrait vessels and the gold ornaments found in the tombs of Sipan.
significance: Moche art is among the finest of the ancient Americas and a main source for understanding Andean society before the Inca.

zh.title: 莫切文化
zh.summary: 秘鲁北岸干旱河谷的莫切人修筑灌溉渠与大型土砖金字塔，例如太阳神庙。他们制作逼真的人物陶器，以及西潘墓葬所见的精美金饰。
zh.significance: 莫切艺术是古代美洲艺术的杰出代表，也是了解印加以前安第斯社会的重要资料。

title: Nazca Lines
summary: On the desert plain of southern Peru, the Nazca people scrape away dark surface stones to make huge figures of animals such as a monkey, a hummingbird and a spider, along with long straight lines and geometric shapes, some best seen from the air. They were made over several centuries, roughly 500 BC to AD 500, and their purpose, perhaps ritual walking paths or links to water and the sky, is still debated.
significance: The lines are among the largest artworks ever made, and their preservation in the dry desert has made them one of the best-known archaeological sites in the Americas.

zh.title: 纳斯卡线条
zh.summary: 秘鲁纳斯卡沙漠的人群移除表面深色石块，在地面形成动物、植物、直线与几何图案。制作持续数百年，其用途仍有争论，可能涉及仪式与水源。
zh.significance: 这些巨型地画展示安第斯社会组织与象征文化，也因干燥气候而保存至今。
zh.dateLabel: 约公元100年（制作于约公元前500年-公元500年）

title: Cai Lun improves papermaking
summary: Cai Lun, an official at the Han court in Luoyang, presents the emperor with paper made from tree bark, hemp, old rags and fishing nets. Simpler kinds of paper already existed in China, but his method made a cheaper, better writing material, and Chinese tradition credits him as the inventor of paper.
significance: Paper gradually replaced bamboo strips and silk in China, then spread to Korea, Japan, the Islamic world and Europe, and later helped make printing and wider literacy possible.

zh.title: 蔡伦改进造纸术
zh.summary: 洛阳汉廷官员蔡伦向皇帝呈献以树皮、麻、旧布和渔网制成的纸。中国此前已有较简单的纸，但他的工艺使纸更廉价、更适合书写，因此传统上常将造纸术归功于他。
zh.significance: 纸逐渐取代竹简与丝帛，随后传到朝鲜、日本、伊斯兰世界和欧洲，为印刷术及读写能力的普及创造条件。

title: Trajan's Column dedicated
summary: A monumental column in Rome commemorates Trajan's Dacian campaigns through a spiraling relief. Its scenes combine military storytelling with imperial self-presentation.
significance: The monument became an influential model of public historical narrative and political commemoration.

zh.title: 图拉真纪功柱落成
zh.summary: 罗马的一座纪念柱以螺旋浮雕纪念图拉真的达契亚战争，将军事叙事与帝国自我呈现相结合。
zh.significance: 它成为公共历史叙事与政治纪念艺术的重要范例。

title: Roman Empire at its greatest extent
summary: When Emperor Trajan dies in 117, his conquests of Dacia (in today's Romania) and, briefly, Armenia and Mesopotamia have stretched Roman rule from Britain to the Persian Gulf. His successor Hadrian soon gives up the eastern conquests and turns to defending the borders.
significance: This marked the peak of Roman territorial expansion; afterward the empire mostly defended what it held, a shift symbolized by Hadrian's Wall in Britain.

zh.title: 罗马帝国疆域达到顶峰
zh.summary: 图拉真皇帝征服达契亚，并进攻帕提亚、占领美索不达米亚，使罗马疆域达到最大。部分东方领土在其死后不久即被放弃。
zh.significance: 这一高峰显示罗马的军事力量，也暴露了远距离统治与防守的极限。

title: Zhang Heng's earthquake detector
summary: At the Han court, Zhang Heng presents an instrument intended to indicate the direction of a distant earthquake. Historical descriptions tell of bronze dragons releasing balls into toad-shaped receivers. The original device does not survive, and its internal mechanism remains debated.
significance: The earliest known seismoscope represents an ambitious attempt to detect natural events beyond direct human perception using an instrument.

zh.title: 张衡制成候风地动仪
zh.summary: 张衡在汉朝宫廷展示用于指示远方地震方向的仪器。史书记载，铜龙吐出小球，由下方的蟾蜍承接。原器没有留存，其内部构造至今仍有争议。
zh.significance: 这是已知最早的地震检测仪器，体现了借助仪器探测人类感官之外自然现象的探索。

title: Ptolemy's Almagest
summary: Claudius Ptolemy, a Greek scholar working in Roman Egypt, writes a great treatise on astronomy, later known by its Arabic name, the Almagest. It describes an Earth-centered universe in which the Sun, Moon and planets move on combinations of circles, with tables for predicting their positions.
significance: Translated into Arabic and later Latin, it remained the standard work of astronomy in the Islamic world and Europe for some 1,400 years, until Copernicus and Kepler replaced its Earth-centered model.

zh.title: 托勒密《天文学大成》
zh.summary: 在罗马统治下的埃及，希腊学者克劳狄乌斯·托勒密写成天文学巨著，后来以阿拉伯语来源的书名《天文学大成》著称。他提出地心宇宙体系，以多重圆周运动解释日月行星，并提供预测位置的表格。
zh.significance: 此书译成阿拉伯文与拉丁文后，在约一千四百年间成为伊斯兰世界和欧洲的天文学标准，直到哥白尼、开普勒体系取而代之。

title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
summary: Zhang Jue, leader of a Taoist-inspired healing movement, launches a vast peasant uprising across northern and eastern China, his followers wearing yellow headscarves. The Han government crushes the main revolt within a year, but only by relying on regional generals and their private armies.
significance: Those generals became warlords who fought over the weakened Han court, a struggle that ended the dynasty in 220 and led to the Three Kingdoms.

zh.title: 黄巾起义
zh.summary: 受道教思想影响的宗教领袖张角发动遍及中国北部和东部的农民起义，追随者以黄巾为标志。汉廷在一年内镇压主要起义，却依赖地方将领及其私人军队。
zh.significance: 这些将领演变为争夺衰弱汉廷的军阀，最终导致汉朝于220年灭亡，并形成三国局面。
zh.locationName: 河北巨鹿（张角的根据地）

title: Champa
summary: Champa was a group of kingdoms of the Cham people along the coast of what is now central and southern Vietnam. Seafarers and traders, they adopted Hinduism and built brick temple towers, and fought long wars with the Khmer and the Vietnamese. Dai Viet took their capital in 1471, and the last Cham territory was annexed in 1832.
significance: Champa was a major station on the sea route between China and India for more than a thousand years.

zh.title: 占婆
zh.summary: 占婆诸王国分布于今越南中南部沿海，参与海上贸易，接受印度教与佛教，建造砖塔神庙。其领土后来逐步被向南扩张的越南政权吞并。
zh.significance: 占婆是连接中国、印度与东南亚的海上文化中心，其后裔和文化传统仍然存在。

title: Cao Cao wins at Guandu
summary: Cao Cao defeats Yuan Shao after a campaign in northern China, including an attack on his rival's supply depot. The victory shifts the balance among warlords as Han central authority collapses.
significance: Guandu laid the groundwork for Cao Cao's dominance in the north and the later Three Kingdoms division.

zh.title: 曹操赢得官渡之战
zh.summary: 曹操在中国北方战役中击败袁绍，袭击对方粮仓成为关键行动。胜利改变了汉朝中央权威瓦解时期的军阀力量对比。
zh.significance: 官渡之战为曹操统一北方与后来三国格局奠定基础。

title: Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan
summary: In the Valley of Mexico, the people of Teotihuacan complete the Pyramid of the Sun, one of the largest structures in the ancient Americas, along the city's great central avenue, later called the Avenue of the Dead. The city is already home to tens of thousands of people, later growing toward 100,000 or more. Its builders' language and name for the city are unknown; 'Teotihuacan' is the name later given by the Aztecs.
significance: Teotihuacan was one of the largest cities in the world at its height, and its trade, art and influence reached as far as the Maya region.

zh.title: 特奥蒂瓦坎太阳金字塔
zh.summary: 特奥蒂瓦坎在今墨西哥谷地建造巨大的太阳金字塔，成为城市规划与宗教空间的中心建筑之一。其建造年代通常定于约公元200年。
zh.significance: 它显示美洲早期城市能够动员庞大劳力，至今仍是该文明最显著的象征之一。

title: Battle of Red Cliffs
summary: The warlord Cao Cao, master of northern China, leads a large army and fleet south to finish off his rivals. The allied forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei, far fewer in number, set his chained ships on fire on the Yangtze and force him to retreat north.
significance: The defeat ended Cao Cao's hope of reuniting China and fixed the three-way division that became the Three Kingdoms; it is one of the most retold battles in Chinese literature.

zh.title: 赤壁之战
zh.summary: 控制北方的曹操率大军与水师南下，试图消灭对手。孙权与刘备的联军人数较少，却在长江上火攻曹军相连的战船，迫使其北撤。
zh.significance: 此败挫折了曹操统一中国的希望，奠定三国鼎立格局，也成为中国文学中最常被讲述的战役之一。
zh.locationName: 长江沿岸赤壁（具体地点有争议）

title: Roman citizenship extended across the empire
summary: Emperor Caracalla grants Roman citizenship to nearly all free inhabitants of the empire. Enslaved people remain excluded, and citizenship does not remove differences of wealth or legal status.
significance: The edict transformed membership in the Roman political community from a selective privilege into a much broader status.

zh.title: 罗马公民权扩大至全帝国
zh.summary: 卡拉卡拉皇帝将罗马公民权授予帝国几乎所有自由居民。被奴役者仍被排除，公民权也未消除财富与法律地位差别。
zh.significance: 法令使罗马政治共同体成员资格从选择性特权转变为更广泛的身份。

title: Three Kingdoms
summary: When the Han dynasty collapsed, China was divided among three rival states: Wei in the north, Shu in the southwest and Wu in the southeast. Decades of war followed until the Jin dynasty briefly reunited the country in 280.
significance: The period opened more than three centuries of division in China, and its generals and strategists became legends through the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms.

zh.title: 三国时期
zh.summary: 汉朝瓦解后，中国分为北方的魏、西南的蜀和东南的吴。数十年战争之后，晋朝于280年短暂统一全国。
zh.significance: 三国开启了中国三百余年的分裂时期，其将领与谋士又通过《三国演义》成为广为流传的人物。

title: Sasanian Empire
summary: Ardashir I overthrew the Parthians and founded a Persian dynasty that ruled Iran and Mesopotamia from Ctesiphon. The Sasanians made Zoroastrianism the state religion and fought Rome and Byzantium for four centuries, until the Arab conquests destroyed the empire.
significance: It was the last Persian empire before Islam, and its court culture, art and administration deeply influenced the caliphates that replaced it.

zh.title: 萨珊帝国
zh.summary: 萨珊王朝取代帕提亚，建立以伊朗和美索不达米亚为核心的中央集权帝国，扶持祆教，与罗马及拜占庭长期交战，最终亡于阿拉伯征服。
zh.significance: 它塑造了伊朗国家与宫廷文化，其行政、艺术和政治传统影响了后来的伊斯兰世界。

title: Queen Himiko sends envoys to China

location.name: Yoshinogari, Kyushu (one proposed site of Yamatai)

summary: A Chinese history, the Records of the Three Kingdoms, reports that Himiko, the shaman queen of Yamatai in the land of Wa, sends envoys to the court of Wei and is recognized as a friendly ruler. Where Yamatai lay, in Kyushu or in the Nara region, has been argued over for centuries.
significance: The account is the earliest detailed description of Japan by any writer and the first record of a named Japanese ruler.

zh.title: 卑弥呼女王遣使中国
zh.summary: 《三国志》记载，倭国邪马台的巫女王卑弥呼遣使到魏廷，并获册封。邪马台究竟位于九州还是奈良一带，数百年来一直存在争论。
zh.significance: 这是目前最早详述日本的文献之一，也是最早记载具体姓名的日本统治者的资料。
zh.locationName: 九州吉野里（可能的邪马台国遗址之一）

title: Classic Maya
summary: In the lowlands of Guatemala, Belize and southern Mexico, Maya city-states such as Tikal, Calakmul, Palenque and Copan were ruled by divine kings. They built stone temples and palaces and recorded their history in a hieroglyphic script with a precise calendar.
significance: The Classic Maya created the most developed writing system of the ancient Americas, along with advanced astronomy and mathematics that included the concept of zero.

zh.title: 玛雅古典时期
zh.summary: 玛雅低地形成蒂卡尔、卡拉克穆尔、帕伦克等竞争城邦，统治者建造金字塔宫殿，以文字和复杂历法记录王朝、战争与仪式。
zh.significance: 此时期是玛雅城市、艺术、天文学与文字文化的高峰，留下古代美洲最丰富的历史记录之一。

title: Classic Maya period begins
summary: In the rainforests of what are now southern Mexico, Guatemala and Belize, Maya city-states such as Tikal, Calakmul, Palenque and Copan flourish under divine kings. They build stone temples and palaces, and record royal history on carved monuments in a hieroglyphic script, using an advanced calendar and a counting system that includes zero.
significance: The Classic Maya created the most fully developed writing system known from the ancient Americas, along with remarkable achievements in astronomy, mathematics and art.

zh.title: 玛雅古典时期开始
zh.summary: 约公元250年起，玛雅低地城市进入古典时期，王朝铭文、石碑和大型建筑增多，蒂卡尔等城邦彼此竞争。
zh.significance: 玛雅的文字、历法、天文和艺术在此时期高度发展，使其成为古代美洲最具代表性的文明之一。

title: Yamato Japan
summary: From the Nara basin, the Yamato rulers gradually brought the clans of western and central Japan under their authority, burying their dead in huge keyhole-shaped mounds. In the 6th and 7th centuries the court adopted Buddhism, Chinese writing and, with the Taika reforms, a Chinese model of centralized government.
significance: The Yamato rulers are the ancestors of Japan's imperial line, and in this period Japan took shape as a single state.

zh.title: 日本大和政权
zh.summary: 大和统治者以奈良盆地为中心，逐步将日本中部和西部氏族纳入统治，并建造巨大的前方后圆坟。6至7世纪，朝廷接受佛教与汉字，又通过大化改新借鉴中国中央集权制度。
zh.significance: 大和统治者是日本皇室世系的祖先，日本也在这一时期逐渐形成统一国家。

title: Liu Hui explains the Nine Chapters
summary: Liu Hui writes a commentary on the Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art, explaining why its procedures work. His work includes geometric reasoning and an algorithm for approximating pi.
significance: The commentary became a foundational work in Chinese mathematical reasoning, extending a much older problem-solving tradition.

zh.title: 刘徽注解《九章算术》
zh.summary: 刘徽为《九章算术》作注，解释各种算法成立的理由，内容包括几何推理与圆周率近似算法。
zh.significance: 注解成为中国数学推理的基础著作，发展了更早的解题传统。
zh.locationName: 中国北方曹魏境内（区域位置）

title: Jin dynasty
summary: The Sima family took the throne of Wei and reunited China in 280, but a war between its princes left the north open to invasion by steppe peoples. From 317 the dynasty survived in the south, ruling from Jiankang, modern Nanjing, while rival kingdoms fought over the north.
significance: The flight of the court and many northern families shifted the center of Chinese culture toward the Yangtze for the first time and helped Buddhism take root in China.

zh.title: 晋朝
zh.summary: 司马氏取代魏，并于280年统一中国，但宗室内战使北方无力抵御草原民族入侵。317年起，晋室在南方延续，定都建康，即今南京，北方则由诸国争夺。
zh.significance: 朝廷与大量北方家族南迁，使中国文化中心首次明显向长江流域转移，也促进了佛教在中国扎根。

title: Ghana Empire
summary: The Ghana Empire, founded by Soninke people in what is now Mauritania and Mali, grew rich by taxing the trade in gold from the south and salt from the Sahara. Arab writers described its king's wealth and its capital at Koumbi Saleh.
significance: It was the first of the great trading empires of the West African Sahel, followed by Mali and Songhai; modern Ghana took its name from it.

zh.title: 加纳帝国
zh.summary: 古加纳帝国位于今毛里塔尼亚和马里一带，与现代加纳并不重合。其统治者控制撒哈拉南缘的黄金、盐及商路，向贸易征税。
zh.significance: 它是西非最早的大帝国之一，将萨赫勒与北非、地中海商业世界连接起来。

title: Luoyang falls in the Yongjia disaster
summary: Forces of the Han-Zhao state capture Luoyang, sack the Jin capital and take Emperor Huai prisoner. The disaster deepens the collapse of Western Jin authority in northern China.
significance: The upheaval accelerated migration south and helped reshape the political and cultural geography of China.

zh.title: 永嘉之乱中洛阳陷落
zh.summary: 汉赵军队攻陷洛阳，劫掠晋都并俘虏晋怀帝，进一步加剧了西晋在中国北方统治的崩溃。
zh.significance: 动荡加速人口南迁，推动重塑中国政治与文化地理。

title: Edict of Milan
summary: Meeting in Milan, the Roman emperors Constantine and Licinius agree to give all people, including Christians, the freedom to worship as they choose, and to return property taken from Christians. It follows the last and harshest persecution of Christians, which an edict of 311 had already ended in part; historians debate whether a formal 'edict' was ever issued in Milan.
significance: With Constantine's backing, Christianity grew from a persecuted minority into the favored religion of the empire, and by 380 its official religion.

zh.title: 《米兰敕令》
zh.summary: 君士坦丁与李锡尼在米兰会面，同意保障包括基督徒在内的宗教信仰自由，并归还教会财产。311年已有宽容措施，所谓“敕令”的正式形式仍有学术争论。
zh.significance: 基督教由受迫害群体逐步转为得到皇帝支持的宗教，并于380年获得帝国国教地位。

title: Gupta Empire
summary: The Gupta kings ruled most of northern India from the Ganges plain. Their court patronized Sanskrit literature, such as the plays of Kalidasa, along with Hindu and Buddhist art and scholars including the astronomer Aryabhata.
significance: The Gupta age is remembered as a classical age of Indian culture, and its mathematicians developed the decimal place-value system with zero that the world now uses.

zh.title: 笈多王朝
zh.summary: 笈多王朝以恒河平原为中心统治北印度大部，宫廷扶持迦梨陀娑等人的梵语文学、印度教与佛教艺术，以及数学和天文学。
zh.significance: 笈多时期被视为印度文化的古典时代，十进位值制等数学传统在这一背景中发展。

title: Gupta Empire founded
summary: Chandragupta I, a king in the Ganges valley, takes the title 'great king of kings' and begins the Gupta era. His successors Samudragupta and Chandragupta II expand the empire across much of northern India.
significance: The Gupta age is often called a classical or golden age of India, with advances in mathematics and astronomy, Sanskrit literature such as Kalidasa's plays, and Hindu and Buddhist art.

zh.title: 笈多王朝建立
zh.summary: 恒河流域君主旃陀罗笈多一世采用大王之王头衔，开启笈多纪元。继任者沙摩陀罗笈多和旃陀罗笈多二世将帝国扩大至北印度大部。
zh.significance: 这一时期常被称为印度文化的黄金时代，文学、艺术、数学和天文学取得重要成就。

title: Council of Nicaea
summary: Emperor Constantine calls Christian bishops from across the empire to Nicaea, in northwestern Anatolia, to settle a bitter dispute over the teachings of Arius, a priest of Alexandria who says Christ the Son was created by God the Father. The council rejects Arius's view and issues a statement of belief, the original Nicene Creed.
significance: It was the first council claiming to speak for the whole church, and the Nicene Creed, in a version expanded in 381, is still recited by most Christian churches.

zh.title: 尼西亚会议
zh.summary: 君士坦丁召集各地主教到尼西亚，处理阿里乌关于圣子由圣父创造的教义争端。会议拒绝该主张，形成最初的《尼西亚信经》。
zh.significance: 这是首次声称代表整个教会的普世会议，381年扩充后的信经至今仍为多数基督教会采用。

title: Aksum adopts Christianity
summary: King Ezana of Aksum converts to Christianity, influenced by Frumentius, a Syrian Christian who had been brought to the royal court as a captive and later became the kingdom's first bishop. Aksum's coins begin to show the cross instead of pagan symbols. The exact date of the conversion is uncertain.
significance: Aksum was among the earliest states to adopt Christianity officially, and the Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox churches trace their origins to this conversion.

zh.title: 阿克苏姆接受基督教
zh.summary: 阿克苏姆王埃扎纳在叙利亚基督徒弗鲁门提乌斯影响下接受基督教，后者曾为宫廷俘虏，后来成为首任主教。钱币开始出现十字架，确切改宗年份未定。
zh.significance: 阿克苏姆成为最早正式接受基督教的国家之一，埃塞俄比亚与厄立特里亚教会均将传统追溯至此。

title: Byzantine Empire
summary: The eastern half of the Roman Empire, ruled from Constantinople, survived the fall of the west by a thousand years. Greek in language and Orthodox Christian in religion, it preserved Roman law and ancient learning while defending itself against Persians, Arabs, Bulgars, crusaders and Turks.
significance: It shielded Europe from the east for centuries, converted the Slavs to Orthodox Christianity, and passed Greek learning on to both the Islamic world and Renaissance Italy.

zh.title: 拜占庭帝国
zh.summary: 以君士坦丁堡为中心的东罗马帝国，在西部灭亡后延续约一千年。它使用希腊语、信奉东正教，保存罗马法律和古典知识，并长期对抗波斯、阿拉伯、十字军与土耳其势力。
zh.significance: 它向斯拉夫世界传播东正教，也将古希腊学术传递给伊斯兰世界与文艺复兴时期的意大利。

title: Constantinople founded
summary: Emperor Constantine dedicates the old Greek city of Byzantium, rebuilt and greatly enlarged, as a new imperial capital named Constantinople. It controls the strait of the Bosporus between Europe and Asia and between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.
significance: Constantinople was the capital of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire for over a thousand years, then of the Ottoman Empire, and as Istanbul remains one of the world's great cities.

zh.title: 君士坦丁堡建立
zh.summary: 君士坦丁将古希腊城市拜占庭大规模扩建，正式设为帝国新都，命名君士坦丁堡。城市扼守博斯普鲁斯海峡，连接欧亚与黑海、地中海。
zh.significance: 它作为东罗马首都延续千余年，后成为奥斯曼首都，如今的伊斯坦布尔仍是世界大城。
zh.locationName: 君士坦丁堡（伊斯坦布尔）

title: Huns move west; Migration Period begins
summary: The Huns, nomadic horse archers whose origins are uncertain, move west across the steppe north of the Caspian Sea, defeating the Alans and then the Goths living north of the Black Sea. In 376 large numbers of Goths flee to the Roman frontier on the Danube and are allowed to cross into the empire.
significance: The Huns' advance is often seen as setting off a chain of movements by Germanic and other peoples into the Roman Empire, the so-called Migration Period, which helped bring down the Western Empire and reshape Europe's map.

zh.title: 匈人西迁，民族大迁徙开始
zh.summary: 起源尚不明确的游牧骑射人群匈人向西越过里海北方草原，击败阿兰人与黑海北部哥特人。376年，大批哥特人渡向多瑙河罗马边境并获准进入。
zh.significance: 匈人西进推动日耳曼及其他民族连锁迁徙，加速西罗马瓦解并重塑欧洲。
zh.locationName: 阿特劳附近里海草原（代表地点）

title: Eastern Jin prevails at the Fei River
summary: Eastern Jin forces defeat an invasion led by Former Qin ruler Fu Jian. The invading coalition breaks apart, frustrating an attempt to reunify China by conquest.
significance: The battle preserved the southern regime and prolonged the political division between north and south.

zh.title: 东晋赢得淝水之战
zh.summary: 东晋军队击败前秦君主苻坚率领的入侵军队。入侵联盟瓦解，以征服统一中国的尝试受挫。
zh.significance: 战役保住了南方政权，延长了南北政治分裂。

title: Northern Wei
summary: The Tuoba clan of the Xianbei, a people from the steppe, founded a state that united northern China in 439. Its rulers sponsored Buddhism on a grand scale, and Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang in 494 and required his court to adopt Chinese dress, language and names.
significance: The Northern Wei showed how conquerors from the steppe could rule China by blending with it, and its land system and Buddhist art influenced the Sui and Tang.

zh.title: 北魏
zh.summary: 草原民族鲜卑的拓跋氏建立北魏，于439年统一中国北方。北魏大力扶持佛教；孝文帝于494年迁都洛阳，要求朝廷采用汉族服饰、语言和姓氏。
zh.significance: 北魏展现了草原征服者通过文化融合治理中国的方式，其土地制度与佛教艺术影响了隋唐。

title: Faxian begins his pilgrimage to India
summary: The Buddhist monk Faxian leaves China to seek monastic texts, traveling through Central Asia to India and returning by sea. His account records religious practices and conditions along the route.
significance: The journey strengthened Buddhist textual exchange and left an important source for the history of Asia.

zh.title: 法显启程赴印度求法
zh.summary: 佛教僧人法显离开中国寻求戒律典籍，经中亚到印度，再由海路返回。他的记述记录了沿途宗教实践与社会状况。
zh.significance: 旅程加强了佛教典籍交流，并留下研究亚洲历史的重要资料。

title: Visigoths sack Rome
summary: The Visigoths, led by their king Alaric, enter Rome and plunder it for three days after the Western Roman government, based at Ravenna, refuses their demands. It is the first time in about 800 years that the city has fallen to a foreign enemy.
significance: The sack shocked the Roman world and prompted Augustine of Hippo to write The City of God, a defense of Christianity that shaped Western thought for centuries.

zh.title: 西哥特人洗劫罗马
zh.summary: 以拉文纳为中心的西罗马政府拒绝要求后，阿拉里克率西哥特人进入罗马，洗劫三天。这是约八百年来罗马首次落入外敌之手。
zh.significance: 洗劫震动罗马世界，促使希波的奥古斯丁撰写《上帝之城》，这部基督教辩护著作影响西方思想数百年。

title: Visigothic Kingdom
summary: The Visigoths, a Germanic people who had sacked Rome in 410, were settled in southern Gaul by the Romans and built a kingdom there. Driven out of most of Gaul by the Franks in 507, they ruled Spain from Toledo and converted from Arian to Catholic Christianity in 589. The kingdom fell to the Umayyad invasion of 711.
significance: It was one of the main successor states of the western Roman Empire, and its law code shaped medieval Spanish law.

zh.title: 西哥特王国
zh.summary: 西哥特人在410年洗劫罗马后，于高卢南部建立王国。507年败于法兰克后，统治重心转到托莱多和西班牙，589年改宗天主教，最终在711年倭马亚入侵后崩溃。
zh.significance: 它是西罗马的重要继承国，其法典对中世纪西班牙法律影响深远。

title: Northern and Southern dynasties
summary: For nearly two centuries China was divided between a north ruled by dynasties of steppe origin and a south ruled by a succession of Chinese dynasties from Jiankang, modern Nanjing. Despite constant war it was an age of creativity in poetry, painting and calligraphy, and Buddhism spread through both halves.
significance: Buddhism became a religion of the whole of China in these centuries, and the south was settled and developed into the country's economic heartland.

zh.title: 南北朝时期
zh.summary: 近两百年间，中国分为由草原民族出身的王朝统治的北方，以及以建康为都城、王朝相继更迭的南方。战乱不断，诗歌、绘画、书法仍富有创造力，佛教在南北广泛传播。
zh.significance: 佛教在此期间成为遍及中国的宗教，南方也随着人口迁入和开发，逐渐成长为经济中心。

title: Nalanda university founded
summary: A great Buddhist monastery and center of learning is founded at Nalanda in eastern India, traditionally under the Gupta king Kumaragupta I. It grows into a large residential community of monks and students who study Buddhist philosophy, logic, grammar and medicine. Calling it a 'university' is a modern comparison, and its founding date is approximate.
significance: Nalanda drew scholars from as far as China, Korea and Central Asia, including the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang, and remained a major center of Buddhist learning until its decline around 1200.

zh.title: 那烂陀寺建立
zh.summary: 印度东部建立了大型佛教寺院与学习中心那烂陀，传统上归于笈多王朝鸠摩罗笈多一世时期。它发展为僧侣与学生共同居住的庞大社群，教授佛学、逻辑、语法与医学。“大学”是现代类比，其创建年代也仅为约数。
zh.significance: 那烂陀吸引中国、朝鲜、中亚等地的学者，包括玄奘，并一直是重要佛学中心，直到约1200年衰落。

title: Council of Chalcedon
summary: A council defines Christ as one person in two natures, divine and human. Several Christian communities reject the formulation, deepening enduring divisions.
significance: Its disputes helped shape the separate histories of Chalcedonian and Oriental Orthodox churches.

zh.title: 迦克墩公会议
zh.summary: 会议将基督界定为一个位格、兼具神性与人性两种本性。一些基督徒群体拒绝这一表述，形成持久分歧。
zh.significance: 相关争论塑造了迦克墩派教会与东方正统教会各自的发展历史。

title: Yungang Grottoes begun
summary: Near their capital at Pingcheng, modern Datong, the Northern Wei emperors have Buddhist cave temples cut into a sandstone cliff under the direction of the monk Tanyao. Over the following decades sculptors carve more than 50,000 figures, from tiny reliefs to seated Buddhas about 17 meters high.
significance: The caves are the first great monument of Buddhist art in China, blending styles from India and Central Asia with Chinese ones.

zh.title: 云冈石窟开凿
zh.summary: 北魏皇帝在首都平城、今大同附近，由僧人昙曜主持，在砂岩崖壁开凿佛教石窟。此后数十年雕刻了五万余尊造像，从微小浮雕到约17米高的坐佛。
zh.significance: 云冈是中国早期最重要的佛教艺术遗存之一，融合了印度、中亚和中国的艺术风格。

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
summary: The Germanic general Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last Western Roman emperor, and rules Italy as king without naming a new emperor. By then the Western Empire had already lost most of its provinces to Germanic kingdoms.
significance: The date is the traditional end of the ancient world in Western Europe, while the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire carries on for nearly another thousand years.

zh.title: 西罗马帝国灭亡
zh.summary: 日耳曼将领奥多亚塞废黜西罗马皇帝罗慕路斯·奥古斯都，以国王身份治理意大利而不另立皇帝。此时西部帝国大部分行省已被日耳曼王国占据。
zh.significance: 476年常被作为西欧古代结束的标志，而东罗马帝国仍继续存在近千年。

title: Zu Chongzhi refines the value of pi
summary: Zu Chongzhi obtains exceptionally close bounds for pi and the approximation 355/113. These achievements are conventionally placed in the fifth century, around 480; his detailed method does not survive.
significance: His results demonstrate the high precision achieved by early Chinese computational mathematics.

zh.title: 祖冲之精算圆周率
zh.summary: 祖冲之得出极为精确的圆周率上下界及355/113近似值。这些成果通常定于5世纪、约480年前后，详细方法未完整留存。
zh.significance: 成果展示了早期中国计算数学达到的高度精确性。

title: Frankish Kingdom
summary: Clovis united the Franks, conquered most of Roman Gaul and accepted Catholic Christianity around 500. His Merovingian descendants reigned for two and a half centuries while real power passed to their chief officials, the mayors of the palace, one of whom, Pippin, took the crown in 751. His son Charlemagne turned the kingdom into an empire.
significance: The Frankish kingdom was the most lasting state to follow Rome in the West, and both France and Germany descend from it.

zh.title: 法兰克王国
zh.summary: 克洛维统一法兰克人，征服罗马高卢大部，并于约500年接受天主教。墨洛温后裔统治两个半世纪，实权逐渐转入宫相手中。751年，宫相丕平夺取王位，其子查理曼又将王国扩展为帝国。
zh.significance: 法兰克是罗马之后西欧延续最久的国家，法国和德国均由其演变而来。

title: Aryabhata's astronomy and mathematics
summary: The Indian astronomer Aryabhata, aged 23 by his own account, completes the Aryabhatiya, a short work in verse on mathematics and astronomy. It works with a place-value number system and gives a value of pi of about 3.1416, early sine tables, and the idea that the Earth spins on its axis.
significance: His work shaped Indian astronomy for centuries and, through Arabic translations, influenced mathematics and astronomy in the Islamic world.

zh.title: 阿耶波多的天文学与数学
zh.summary: 印度天文学家阿耶波多自述23岁时完成《阿耶波多历数书》，论述数学与天文，使用位值制，给出约3.1416的圆周率和早期正弦表，并提出地球绕轴自转。
zh.significance: 其著作影响印度天文学数百年，又经阿拉伯文翻译传播到伊斯兰世界。
zh.locationName: 拘苏摩补罗（可能为华氏城）

title: Code of Justinian
summary: Emperor Justinian I issues the first version of a new code that gathers and simplifies centuries of Roman imperial laws. Over the next few years his commission, led by the jurist Tribonian, adds a digest of Roman legal writings and a textbook for students, the whole later called the Corpus Juris Civilis.
significance: Rediscovered in Italy in the 11th century, it became the foundation of the civil law systems used across much of continental Europe, Latin America and beyond.

zh.title: 《查士丁尼法典》
zh.summary: 查士丁尼一世颁布新法典首版，汇集并整理数百年罗马帝国法律。此后，由特里波尼安主持的委员会又编成法学著作摘要与教材，合称《民法大全》。
zh.significance: 11世纪在意大利重新受到重视后，它成为欧洲大陆、拉丁美洲及其他广大地区大陆法体系的基础。

title: Rule of Saint Benedict
summary: Benedict develops a rule for monastic community life balancing prayer, work and study. Its composition is conventionally placed in the sixth century, around 530.
significance: The rule became a major framework for western monasticism and institutions that preserved texts and learning.

zh.title: 《圣本笃会规》形成
zh.summary: 本笃制定修道共同生活的规则，协调祈祷、劳动与学习。成书通常定于6世纪、约530年前后。
zh.significance: 会规成为西欧修道制度的重要框架，相关机构保存了文献与学术。

title: Hagia Sophia completed
summary: After a riot destroys the previous church, Emperor Justinian has the architects Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus build a new Hagia Sophia ('Holy Wisdom') in Constantinople in under six years. Its enormous dome seems to float above a ring of windows.
significance: For centuries it was the largest church in the Christian world; after 1453 it became a mosque whose design inspired Ottoman architects, and it remains a landmark of world architecture.

zh.title: 圣索菲亚大教堂建成
zh.summary: 旧教堂在暴乱中被毁后，查士丁尼皇帝不到六年就在君士坦丁堡重建圣索菲亚大教堂。巨大的穹顶仿佛悬浮在一圈窗户之上。
zh.significance: 它曾是基督教世界最大的教堂，1453年后改为清真寺，设计影响了奥斯曼建筑师，至今仍是世界建筑史的里程碑。
zh.locationName: 君士坦丁堡圣索菲亚大教堂

title: Plague of Justinian
summary: Bubonic plague appears at Pelusium in Egypt in 541 and reaches Constantinople the next year, where contemporaries report thousands of deaths a day. DNA from victims' remains confirms it was caused by the same bacterium as the later Black Death. The plague keeps returning for some two centuries, and how many people it killed is still debated.
significance: It is the first well-documented outbreak of bubonic plague, and it may have weakened the Byzantine Empire just as Justinian tried to win back the West.

zh.title: 查士丁尼瘟疫
zh.summary: 541年，鼠疫出现在埃及佩鲁西乌姆，翌年传至君士坦丁堡，当时的记述称每日有数千人死亡。遗骸DNA证实，它与后来的黑死病由同一种细菌引起。疫情反复约两百年，死亡规模仍有争论。
zh.significance: 这是有详细记载的第一次鼠疫大流行，削弱了拜占庭帝国，可能也影响了地中海世界后来的力量格局。

title: Jia Sixie compiles Essential Techniques for the People
summary: Jia Sixie compiles practical knowledge of farming, animal husbandry, food processing and household production. The agricultural treatise is generally dated to around 544.
significance: The book preserved detailed agricultural techniques and became one of China's most influential farming manuals.

zh.title: 贾思勰编成《齐民要术》
zh.summary: 贾思勰汇集耕作、畜牧、食品加工与家庭生产的实用知识。这部农书通常定于约544年。
zh.significance: 著作保存了详细农业技术，成为中国最具影响力的农书之一。

title: Buddhism reaches Japan
summary: According to the Nihon Shoki, an early Japanese chronicle, King Seong of the Korean kingdom of Baekje sends a Buddhist statue and scriptures to the Japanese court. Other sources give the date as 538. The new religion is opposed by some powerful clans but supported by the Soga clan, and later by Prince Shotoku.
significance: Buddhism became, alongside Shinto, one of Japan's two main religious traditions, bringing temples such as Horyu-ji, art and learning from the Asian mainland.

zh.title: 佛教传入日本
zh.summary: 《日本书纪》记载，百济圣王向日本朝廷赠送佛像与经书，另有文献将此事定于538年。部分氏族反对新宗教，苏我氏与后来的圣德太子则支持它。
zh.significance: 佛教与神道一起成为日本主要宗教传统，并带来大陆的寺院建筑、艺术与学术。
zh.dateLabel: 公元552年（传统说法；部分文献记为538年）

title: Gokturk Khaganate
summary: The Turks overthrew their Rouran overlords and founded a khaganate that soon reached from Mongolia to the Black Sea, before splitting into eastern and western halves. After a period of Tang rule, a second khaganate revived Turkic power until 744.
significance: It was the first state to call itself Turk, and its Orkhon inscriptions are the oldest surviving texts in a Turkic language.

zh.title: 突厥汗国
zh.summary: 突厥人推翻柔然，建立横跨蒙古至黑海的汗国，随后分裂为东西两部。经历唐朝控制时期后，第二汗国再次兴起，延续至744年。
zh.significance: 这是第一个以“突厥”为名的国家，鄂尔浑碑铭也是现存最早的重要突厥语文献。

title: Life of Muhammad (approx.)
summary: Muhammad preached Islam in western Arabia and established a community at Medina after the migration of 622. His religious and political leadership laid the foundations for the subsequent caliphates. His birth year is approximate.
significance: Muslims regard him as the last prophet of God; the faith he preached and the community he founded grew into one of the world's largest religions and a civilization spanning three continents.

zh.title: 穆罕默德生平（约）
zh.summary: 穆罕默德在阿拉伯西部传教，622年迁徙后于麦地那建立共同体，以宗教与政治领袖身份为后来的哈里发政权奠定基础。出生年份为约数。
zh.significance: 穆斯林将其视为最后的先知，他创立的信仰与共同体后来发展为世界主要宗教及横跨三洲的文明。

title: Sui dynasty
summary: The Sui reunited China after more than three centuries of division. Its two emperors rebuilt the Great Wall, dug the Grand Canal linking the Yellow River and the Yangtze, and exhausted the country with forced labor and failed wars in Korea.
significance: Short as it was, the Sui restored a united empire and built the canal and institutions on which the Tang dynasty's prosperity rested.

zh.title: 隋朝
zh.summary: 隋朝结束了中国三百余年的分裂。两位皇帝修筑长城，开凿连接黄河与长江的大运河，但繁重劳役和对高句丽的失败战争也耗尽国力。
zh.significance: 隋虽短暂，却恢复了统一，并以运河和制度建设为唐朝繁荣奠定基础。

title: Bhakti devotional traditions
summary: Poet-saints express devotion to Hindu deities in regional languages, beginning with influential Tamil traditions and later flourishing across India. This approximate span covers diverse movements, not a single organization or a fixed beginning and end.
significance: Devotional poetry expanded religious participation and enriched regional literatures, sometimes challenging caste and ritual authority.

zh.title: 巴克提虔信传统
zh.summary: 诗人圣徒以地方语言表达对印度教神祇的虔敬，从有影响力的泰米尔传统发展到印度各地。这一大致时间范围涵盖多种运动，并非单一组织，也没有统一的起止。
zh.significance: 虔信诗歌扩大了宗教参与，丰富地方文学，并在一些传统中挑战种姓与仪式权威。

title: Chaturanga, an ancestor of chess
summary: A strategy game known as chaturanga develops in India around the sixth century. Its exact origins are uncertain; related forms travel to Persia and beyond.
significance: The game lies in the ancestry of chess and illustrates the movement of ideas and recreation across cultures.

zh.title: 国际象棋前身恰图兰卡
zh.summary: 一种名为恰图兰卡的策略棋戏约在6世纪的印度发展。确切起源尚不明晰；相关形式随后传入波斯及其他地区。
zh.significance: 它是国际象棋的前身之一，展示了观念与娱乐方式的跨文化传播。

title: Tiwanaku
summary: Tiwanaku was a city and state near Lake Titicaca, nearly 4,000 meters above sea level, known for monumental stonework such as the Gateway of the Sun. It fed a large population with raised-field farming and spread its influence across the southern Andes.
significance: It was one of the first large states of the Andean highlands, and the Inca later honored its ruins as the place of their own origins.

zh.title: 蒂瓦纳库
zh.summary: 蒂瓦纳库位于的的喀喀湖附近、海拔近四千米的高原，以太阳门等巨石建筑闻名。高畦农业支撑较大人口，影响扩展至安第斯南部。
zh.significance: 它是安第斯高原早期大国之一，印加人后来将其遗址尊为自身起源之地。

title: Imperial examinations begin
summary: The Sui dynasty begins selecting some officials through written examinations open to candidates recommended from across the empire, rather than by birth alone. The Tang expand the system, and under the Song it becomes the main route into government, testing knowledge of the Confucian classics.
significance: For 1,300 years, until 1905, the examinations shaped Chinese education and society around the ideal of rule by scholars, and they inspired civil service examinations elsewhere.

zh.title: 科举制度兴起
zh.summary: 隋朝开始通过笔试选拔部分由各地推荐的官员，而非完全依据门第。唐朝扩展这一制度，宋朝时它成为入仕的主要途径，考查内容以儒家经典为中心。
zh.significance: 直到1905年废除，科举在约一千三百年间围绕士人治国的理想塑造了中国教育与社会，也影响了其他地区的文官考试。

title: Sui dynasty builds the Grand Canal

location.name: Luoyang (hub of the Sui canal network)

summary: Emperor Yang of the Sui dynasty orders millions of laborers to dig and link canals joining the Yellow River and the Yangtze, connecting the rich farmlands of the south with the political centers of the north. Parts of the system already existed, and most of the work is finished within a few years.
significance: Expanded by later dynasties, the Grand Canal became the longest artificial waterway in the world and a lifeline of China's economy, though its huge cost in forced labor helped bring down the Sui in 618.

zh.title: 隋朝开凿大运河
zh.summary: 隋炀帝征发数百万劳工，开凿并连接运河，使黄河与长江贯通，将南方富庶农区与北方政治中心相连。部分河段已有基础，大部分工程在数年内完成。
zh.significance: 后世继续扩建的大运河成为世界上最长的人工水道和中国经济命脉，但沉重劳役也加速了隋朝在618年的灭亡。
zh.locationName: 洛阳（隋朝运河网络枢纽）

title: Zhaozhou Bridge completed
summary: Builders led by Li Chun complete a stone bridge with a shallow main arch and smaller openings above it. Construction is usually dated to 595-605 under the Sui.
significance: The surviving bridge is an outstanding example of early open-spandrel stone-arch engineering.

zh.title: 赵州桥建成
zh.summary: 李春主持建成一座采用平缓主拱、拱肩另设小拱的石桥，工程通常定于隋代595至605年。
zh.significance: 这座留存至今的桥梁是早期敞肩石拱工程的杰出范例。

title: Harsha's empire in North India
summary: Harsha becomes king of Thanesar at the age of about 16 and soon also rules Kannauj, which he makes his capital. Through wars and alliances he dominates much of northern India, though his advance south is stopped by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II.
significance: Harsha's reign is well described by his court poet Bana and the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang; after his death northern India split into rival kingdoms, and for some time no single ruler from the region held such a large realm.

zh.title: 北印度戒日王帝国
zh.summary: 戒日王约十六岁时继承塔内萨尔王位，很快又统治曲女城并以此为都。他通过征战与结盟控制北印度大部，但南进被遮娄其王朝补罗稽舍二世阻止。
zh.significance: 宫廷诗人波那和中国僧人玄奘详细记述了其统治。他死后北印度重新分裂，此后一段时间无人再统治如此广阔的地区。

title: Horyu-ji temple founded
summary: Prince Shotoku, regent of Japan and a devoted patron of Buddhism, founds the temple of Horyu-ji near his palace at Ikaruga. The original buildings burn in 670 and are rebuilt over the following decades.
significance: Its pagoda and main hall are the oldest wooden buildings still standing in the world, and they preserve the architecture of 7th-century China and Korea.

zh.title: 法隆寺建立
zh.summary: 信奉佛教的摄政圣德太子在斑鸠宫殿附近创建法隆寺。原建筑于670年遭火灾，此后数十年陆续重建。
zh.significance: 其塔与金堂是世界现存最古老的木构建筑，保存了7世纪东亚建筑传统。

title: Muhammad's first revelation
summary: According to Islamic tradition, Muhammad, a merchant of Mecca aged about 40, is meditating in a cave on Mount Hira when the angel Gabriel appears and commands him to 'Recite!'. These words begin the revelations that Muslims believe continue for the rest of his life and are collected in the Quran.
significance: It marks the beginning of Islam, which grew into one of the world's largest religions, with nearly two billion followers today.

zh.title: 穆罕默德首次获得启示
zh.summary: 伊斯兰传统记载，约四十岁的麦加商人穆罕默德在希拉山洞冥想时，天使吉卜利勒显现并命令他“诵读”。穆斯林相信，启示此后延续其余生，并汇集为《古兰经》。
zh.significance: 这标志着伊斯兰教的开端。它后来成为世界最大的宗教之一，信徒接近二十亿。

title: Tang dynasty
summary: The Tang ruled from Chang'an, then one of the largest cities in the world, over an empire reaching far into Central Asia. Its early centuries were an age of poetry, painting, Buddhism and trade along the Silk Road; the An Lushan rebellion later weakened it.
significance: The Tang is remembered as a golden age of Chinese civilization, and its laws, writing and culture became models for Korea, Japan and Vietnam.

zh.title: 唐朝
zh.summary: 唐朝以长安为都，疆域深入中亚。长安是当时世界最大的城市之一。前期诗歌、绘画、佛教及丝绸之路贸易繁荣，安史之乱后国势转弱。
zh.significance: 唐被视为中国文明的黄金时代，其法律、文字与文化成为朝鲜、日本和越南学习的范本。

title: Tang dynasty founded
summary: Li Yuan, a general of the collapsing Sui dynasty, seizes power and founds the Tang with its capital at Chang'an. The city grows into one of the largest and most cosmopolitan in the world, at the eastern end of the Silk Road.
significance: The Tang is remembered as a golden age of Chinese poetry, art and trade, and its culture and institutions shaped Korea, Japan and Vietnam.

zh.title: 唐朝建立
zh.summary: 隋末将领李渊夺取政权，建立唐朝，定都长安。这座位于丝绸之路东端的城市发展为世界上规模最大、文化最为多元的都市之一。
zh.significance: 唐朝被视为中国诗歌、艺术与贸易的黄金时代，其文化和制度深刻影响了朝鲜、日本与越南。

title: Tibetan Empire
summary: Songtsen Gampo united the Tibetan plateau, founded Lhasa and married princesses from China and Nepal, who by tradition brought Buddhism with them. His successors fought Tang China for control of the Silk Road oases and briefly occupied the Tang capital in 763. The empire broke apart after the assassination of its last king in 842.
significance: At its height Tibet was one of the great powers of Asia, and in these centuries it adopted the Buddhism and the script that define its culture.

zh.title: 吐蕃帝国
zh.summary: 松赞干布统一青藏高原，以拉萨为中心，迎娶唐朝与尼泊尔公主；传统认为她们推动佛教传播。继任者与唐争夺丝路绿洲，763年曾短暂攻占长安。末代赞普842年遇刺后帝国瓦解。
zh.significance: 吐蕃鼎盛时是亚洲强国之一，佛教与藏文也在这一时期成为其文化的重要基础。

title: The Hijra to Medina
summary: Facing growing hostility in Mecca, Muhammad's followers move in small groups to the oasis town of Yathrib, later called Medina, and in 622, according to tradition, Muhammad slips out of Mecca secretly with his companion Abu Bakr to join them. In Medina he becomes the town's leader, and an agreement traditionally called the Constitution of Medina sets out the rights and duties of its Muslim, Jewish and other communities.
significance: The Islamic calendar counts its years from the Hijra, which marks the start of Islam as a political as well as religious community.

zh.title: 希吉拉：迁徙麦地那
zh.summary: 面对麦加日益加深的敌意，穆罕默德的追随者分批迁往叶斯里卜，后称麦地那。传统记载，622年穆罕默德与阿布·伯克尔秘密离开麦加前往会合，并成为当地领袖。“麦地那宪章”规定了穆斯林、犹太人及其他群体的权利义务。
zh.significance: 伊斯兰历以此次迁徙为纪元，它标志着伊斯兰教作为政治与宗教共同体的形成。

title: Xuanwu Gate coup brings Taizong to power
summary: Li Shimin kills his rival brothers in a palace coup and soon succeeds his father as Emperor Taizong. The violent succession precedes a reign later celebrated for effective government.
significance: The coup shaped Tang leadership and the contested relationship between dynastic legitimacy and political achievement.

zh.title: 玄武门之变后唐太宗即位
zh.summary: 李世民在宫廷政变中杀死与其竞争的兄弟，随后继承父位成为唐太宗。这场暴力继承发生在后来以治理成就著称的统治之前。
zh.significance: 政变改变了唐朝领导层，也体现王朝合法性与政治成就之间的复杂关系。

title: Brahmagupta sets out arithmetic with zero
summary: Brahmagupta writes the Brahmasphutasiddhanta, setting out rules for calculating with zero and negative numbers. He treats a number minus itself as zero and explains arithmetic using debts and fortunes. His rules for division by zero are not correct by modern standards.
significance: Treating zero as a number that participates in arithmetic, rather than only a placeholder, helped establish a foundation of modern mathematics.

zh.title: 婆罗摩笈多阐述零的运算法则
zh.summary: 婆罗摩笈多撰写《梵天悉檀多》，阐述零与负数的运算法则。他把一个数减去自身的结果定义为零，并用债务与财产解释运算。按现代数学标准，他关于除以零的规则并不正确。
zh.significance: 把零视为可以参与运算的数，而不只是占位符，有助于奠定现代数学的基础。

title: Xuanzang's journey to India

location.name: Chang'an (start and end of the journey)

summary: The Chinese monk Xuanzang slips out of Tang China without permission and travels across the deserts and mountains of Central Asia to India in search of authentic Buddhist scriptures. He studies for years at the monastery of Nalanda and returns with more than 600 texts, which he spends the rest of his life translating.
significance: His translations shaped East Asian Buddhism, and his detailed account of the lands he crossed is a prime source for the history of India and Central Asia; it also inspired the novel Journey to the West.

zh.title: 玄奘西行求法
zh.summary: 僧人玄奘未经许可离开唐朝，穿越中亚沙漠与群山，赴印度寻求可靠佛经。他在那烂陀寺学习多年，带回六百余部经典，并将余生用于翻译。
zh.significance: 其译经影响了东亚佛教，旅行记录成为研究印度与中亚的重要史料，旅程也启发了小说《西游记》。

title: Early Islamic conquests
summary: After Muhammad's death, the first caliphs unite Arabia and send armies against the Byzantine and Sasanian empires, both worn out by decades of war with each other. Within about thirty years the Arabs take Syria, Iraq, Egypt and most of Iran, bringing the Sasanian Empire to an end. Most people in the conquered lands convert to Islam only gradually, over the following centuries.
significance: The conquests created a new empire stretching from North Africa to Iran, in which Arabic and Islam spread and lasting borders between the Muslim and Christian worlds took shape.

zh.title: 早期伊斯兰征服
zh.summary: 穆罕默德死后，早期哈里发统一阿拉伯，进攻因长期战争而衰弱的拜占庭与萨珊。约三十年内，叙利亚、伊拉克、埃及与伊朗大部被征服；当地多数人则在其后数百年逐步改宗。
zh.significance: 征服建立了从北非至伊朗的新帝国，传播阿拉伯语和伊斯兰教，并重塑穆斯林与基督教世界的边界。
zh.locationName: 麦地那（早期哈里发政权首都）

title: Rashidun Caliphate
summary: After Muhammad's death, the first four caliphs, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, led the Muslim community from Medina. In three decades their armies took Syria, Egypt, Iraq and Iran, defeating the Byzantine Empire and destroying the Sasanian one.
significance: Their conquests created an Islamic empire in a single generation, and the disputes over the succession to Ali began the division between Sunni and Shia Islam.

zh.title: 正统哈里发时期
zh.summary: 穆罕默德之后，阿布·伯克尔、欧麦尔、奥斯曼和阿里四位哈里发领导穆斯林共同体。三十年间，军队夺取叙利亚、埃及、伊拉克与伊朗，重创拜占庭并终结萨珊。
zh.significance: 这些征服在一代人间建立伊斯兰帝国，围绕阿里继承权的争端也开启了逊尼派与什叶派的分化。

title: Taika reforms in Japan
summary: Prince Naka no Oe and Nakatomi no Kamatari overthrow the powerful Soga clan in a palace coup and launch reforms to build a centralized state on the Chinese Tang model, with land owned by the throne, a census and taxes collected by officials. How much of the reform edict recorded in the Nihon Shoki dates from this time is debated.
significance: The reforms helped turn the Yamato kingdom into a centralized imperial state ruled by law codes, and Kamatari's descendants, the Fujiwara clan, dominated the Japanese court for centuries.

zh.title: 日本大化改新
zh.summary: 中大兄皇子与中臣镰足发动宫廷政变，推翻强大的苏我氏，开始仿照唐朝建立中央集权国家，推行土地归国家、官员代替世袭氏族首领治理等改革。
zh.significance: 这些改革削弱了旧氏族权力，奠定日本律令国家的制度基础。

title: Khazar Khaganate
summary: The Khazars, a Turkic people, ruled the steppe between the Black and Caspian seas and taxed the trade that crossed it. They stopped the Arab advance north of the Caucasus, and their ruling class adopted Judaism in the 8th or 9th century. The Rus prince Sviatoslav destroyed their capital in the 960s.
significance: The Khazars shielded eastern Europe from the Arab conquests, and their choice of Judaism is unique among steppe empires.

zh.title: 可萨汗国
zh.summary: 突厥语族的可萨人统治黑海与里海之间的草原，征收商路税，并阻止阿拉伯军队越过高加索。统治阶层在8或9世纪接受犹太教，首都于10世纪60年代遭罗斯军摧毁。
zh.significance: 可萨阻挡了阿拉伯向东欧扩张，其选择犹太教也在草原帝国中别具一格。

title: Srivijaya
summary: From Palembang on Sumatra, the Buddhist kingdom of Srivijaya controlled the Strait of Malacca and the Sunda Strait, the sea lanes between India and China. It grew rich on trade and was a center of Buddhist learning visited by Chinese and Indian monks.
significance: For some six centuries it dominated the maritime trade of Southeast Asia and linked the economies of the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.

zh.title: 室利佛逝
zh.summary: 以苏门答腊巨港为中心的室利佛逝控制马六甲与巽他海峡，通过印度和中国间的海上贸易致富，并成为中印僧侣往来的佛学中心。
zh.significance: 它在约六百年间主导东南亚海上贸易，连接印度洋与南海经济。

title: Umayyad Caliphate
summary: The Umayyad family made the caliphate hereditary and ruled it from Damascus. Under them Muslim rule expanded west across North Africa into Spain and east to Central Asia and the Indus, Arabic became the language of government, and the Dome of the Rock was built.
significance: The Umayyads turned the Arab conquests into a lasting empire, the largest the world had yet seen, and a branch of the family later ruled Muslim Spain.

zh.title: 倭马亚王朝
zh.summary: 倭马亚家族使哈里发职位世袭，定都大马士革。穆斯林统治向西跨越北非进入西班牙，向东扩展至中亚与印度河地区。阿拉伯语成为行政语言，圆顶清真寺也在此时建成。
zh.significance: 倭马亚将阿拉伯征服转化为持久帝国，成为当时世界最大的帝国。其一支后裔后来统治穆斯林西班牙。

title: Silla unifies Korea
summary: In alliance with Tang China, the kingdom of Silla destroys Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668. When the Tang try to keep the conquered lands for themselves, Silla fights its former ally and by 676 has driven the Tang armies north of the Taedong River.
significance: Most of the Korean Peninsula came under a single ruler for the first time, while the northern lands of Goguryeo passed to the new kingdom of Balhae.

zh.title: 新罗统一朝鲜半岛大部
zh.summary: 新罗与唐结盟，660年灭百济、668年灭高句丽。唐试图保有征服地区后，新罗转而与其交战，到676年将唐军驱至大同江以北。
zh.significance: 半岛大部首次归于一个政权，高句丽北方故地后来则由渤海国继承。

title: Battle of Karbala
summary: Husayn ibn Ali, a grandson of Muhammad, and his small party are killed by forces of the Umayyad caliph Yazid. Their deaths become a focus of mourning and political memory.
significance: Karbala became central to Shia religious identity and to ideas of resistance against unjust authority.

zh.title: 卡尔巴拉之战
zh.summary: 穆罕默德的外孙侯赛因·伊本·阿里及其少量追随者被倭马亚哈里发叶齐德的军队杀害。他们的死亡成为哀悼与政治记忆的核心。
zh.significance: 卡尔巴拉成为什叶派宗教认同及反抗不义权威观念的核心。

title: Wu Zetian becomes emperor
summary: Wu Zetian, who has governed Tang China for decades as empress consort and then as regent for her sons, sets them aside and takes the throne herself, proclaiming a new Zhou dynasty. She rules until a palace coup removes her in 705, shortly before her death.
significance: She is the only woman to have ruled China as emperor in her own name; her reign widened the examination system and promoted officials from outside the old aristocracy.

zh.title: 武则天称帝
zh.summary: 武则天先以皇后、后以皇太后身份掌权数十年，继而废黜儿子，自立为帝，改国号为周。705年宫廷政变迫使她退位，同年去世。
zh.significance: 她是中国唯一以自身名义称帝的女性。其统治扩大了科举选拔，并提拔旧贵族之外的官员。

title: Republic of Venice
summary: Venice grew from a refuge in a lagoon into a republic governed by an elected doge and a closed circle of merchant families. Its galleys carried the trade between Europe and the eastern Mediterranean, and it held an empire of ports and islands from the Adriatic to Cyprus. Napoleon ended the republic in 1797.
significance: For centuries Venice was the richest trading city in Europe and its main link to the Byzantine and Islamic worlds.

zh.title: 威尼斯共和国
zh.summary: 威尼斯从潟湖避难聚落发展为由选举总督与商人家族治理的共和国，凭海运贸易控制亚得里亚海至塞浦路斯的港口和岛屿，1797年被拿破仑终结。
zh.significance: 它长期是欧洲最富有的商贸城市，也是欧洲联系拜占庭与伊斯兰世界的重要纽带。

title: Balhae
summary: Balhae was founded by Dae Jo-yeong, a former general of Goguryeo, and ruled Manchuria, northern Korea and the coast of what is now the Russian Far East. It adopted Tang institutions, traded with Japan, and was known in China as the flourishing land of the East before it fell to the Khitan.
significance: Balhae carried on the legacy of Goguryeo in the north; both Korea and China count it as part of their history.

zh.title: 渤海国
zh.summary: 原高句丽将领大祚荣建立渤海国，统治满洲、朝鲜半岛北部与今俄罗斯远东沿海。渤海采用唐制，与日本贸易，被誉为“海东盛国”，后来亡于契丹。
zh.significance: 渤海在北方延续了高句丽遗产，朝鲜半岛与中国的历史叙述都将其视为自身历史的一部分。

title: Kanem-Bornu
summary: The kingdom of Kanem grew up northeast of Lake Chad, at the southern end of a trade route across the Sahara, and its rulers adopted Islam in the 11th century. Driven from Kanem in the 14th century, the dynasty rebuilt its state in Bornu, west of the lake, where it reached its height under Idris Alooma around 1600.
significance: A single dynasty, the Sayfawa, ruled it for most of that time, one of the longest reigns of any ruling house in history.

zh.title: 加涅姆-博尔努
zh.summary: 加涅姆兴起于乍得湖东北、撒哈拉商路南端，统治者于11世纪接受伊斯兰教。14世纪王朝西迁博尔努，约1600年在伊德里斯·阿洛马治下达到高峰。
zh.significance: 赛法瓦王朝延续了其中大部分时期，是历史上统治时间最长的王朝之一。

title: Medieval trans-Saharan trade
summary: Caravan networks link West African markets with North Africa, carrying gold, salt, books and enslaved people. The dates mark a broad medieval phase; desert trade existed earlier and continued afterward.
significance: These exchanges supported powerful African states and carried Islam and scholarship across the Sahara.

zh.title: 中世纪跨撒哈拉贸易
zh.summary: 商队网络把西非市场与北非连接起来，运送黄金、盐、书籍和被奴役者。这里标示中世纪的一个大致阶段；沙漠贸易此前已存在，此后也继续进行。
zh.significance: 这些交流支持了强大的非洲国家，并推动伊斯兰教与学术跨越撒哈拉传播。

title: Nara period
summary: Japan's court settled at Heijo-kyo, modern Nara, its first lasting capital, laid out on the model of the Tang capital Chang'an. The state compiled law codes and the first histories of Japan, the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, and poets wrote the verses collected in the Man'yoshu.
significance: In these decades Japan became a literate, centralized state on the Chinese model, with Buddhism established as a religion of the court.

zh.title: 奈良时期
zh.summary: 日本朝廷定都平城京，即今奈良。这座仿照唐都长安布局的城市，是日本首个长期使用的都城。国家编纂律令、《古事记》《日本书纪》等史书，诗歌则汇为《万叶集》。
zh.significance: 日本在这一时期逐渐形成借鉴中国制度、拥有文字文化的中央集权国家，佛教也成为宫廷的重要宗教。

title: Umayyad conquest of Iberia
summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad, a Berber commander serving the Umayyad caliphate, crosses from North Africa at Gibraltar, which is named after him (Jabal Tariq, 'Tariq's mountain'). He defeats the Visigothic king Roderic, and within a few years Muslim forces control most of the Iberian Peninsula.
significance: Muslim-ruled al-Andalus, centered on Cordoba, became a meeting place of Islamic, Jewish and Christian culture, until the Christian kingdoms of the north completed their reconquest in 1492.

zh.title: 倭马亚王朝征服伊比利亚
zh.summary: 为倭马亚效力的柏柏尔将领塔里克·伊本·齐亚德渡海，击败西哥特王罗德里克，数年内控制伊比利亚大部。直布罗陀之名源于“塔里克之山”。
zh.significance: 穆斯林统治的安达卢斯成为伊斯兰、犹太与基督教文化交流地区，最后一个政权直到1492年才被征服。

title: Arab conquest of Sindh
summary: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, a young Umayyad general, captures the port of Debal near the mouth of the Indus, defeats King Dahir of Sindh and takes control of Sindh and southern Punjab, in today's Pakistan. Most of the detailed story comes from the Chach Nama, a Persian chronicle written some five centuries later, whose reliability historians debate.
significance: Sindh became the first lasting foothold of Muslim rule in South Asia, linking the Indus region to the trade and scholarship of the Islamic world.

zh.title: 阿拉伯人征服信德
zh.summary: 年轻将领穆罕默德·伊本·卡西姆攻占印度河口附近港口，击败信德国王，控制今巴基斯坦的信德和旁遮普南部。详细叙述多来自五百年后写成的《查赫纳玛》，可靠性仍有争论。
zh.significance: 信德成为穆斯林在南亚第一个持久统治据点，将印度河地区与伊斯兰贸易和学术网络连接。
zh.locationName: 今卡拉奇附近代布尔（地点未定）

title: Nihon Shoki completed
summary: The Japanese court completes a history written in classical Chinese, combining origin traditions with accounts of rulers and diplomacy. Its narratives express the interests of the early state.
significance: The chronicle became a foundational source for Japanese history and for understanding how the court constructed its past.

zh.title: 《日本书纪》编成
zh.summary: 日本朝廷完成以汉文书写的历史，将起源传说与君主、外交记述结合，其叙事体现早期国家的立场。
zh.significance: 这部编年史成为研究日本历史及朝廷如何建构过去的基础资料。

title: Battle of Tours

location.name: Between Tours and Poitiers (exact site uncertain)

summary: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeat an Umayyad army from al-Andalus led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, who is killed in the battle, somewhere between Poitiers and Tours in western France. Some historians date the battle to 733.
significance: Later writers often hailed it as saving Christian Europe from Islamic conquest, a view many historians now consider exaggerated, but it strengthened Charles Martel's family, the Carolingians.

zh.title: 图尔战役
zh.summary: 查理·马特率法兰克军在图尔与普瓦捷之间击败来自安达卢斯的倭马亚军，敌军统帅战死。部分学者将战役定于733年。
zh.significance: 后世常称其“拯救基督教欧洲”，现代研究多认为这种说法夸大，但胜利确实强化了加洛林家族。
zh.locationName: 图尔与普瓦捷之间（具体地点未定）

title: Kul Tigin inscription erected
summary: A memorial to the Turkic prince Kul Tigin records the fortunes of the Turks in Old Turkic and Chinese. A related monument honors Bilge Qaghan in 735.
significance: These monuments preserve some of the earliest substantial Turkic texts and a steppe ruling elite's own account of its past.

zh.title: 阙特勤碑建立
zh.summary: 纪念突厥王子阙特勤的碑文以古突厥文和汉文记录突厥历史。相关的毗伽可汗碑于735年建立。
zh.significance: 这些碑铭保存了最早的一批长篇突厥语文本，以及草原统治精英对自身历史的叙述。

title: Uyghur Khaganate
summary: The Uyghurs overthrew the Gokturks and ruled Mongolia for a century from their capital on the Orkhon River. They helped the Tang dynasty put down the An Lushan Rebellion in return for a lucrative trade of horses for silk, and their rulers adopted Manichaeism. The Kyrgyz destroyed the khaganate in 840, and the Uyghurs moved south to the oases of the Tarim Basin.
significance: It was the first steppe empire to build cities and adopt a world religion, and its heirs gave the Mongols their script.

zh.title: 回鹘汗国
zh.summary: 回鹘推翻突厥，在蒙古高原统治近百年，以鄂尔浑河畔为都。它帮助唐平定安史之乱，换取有利的马绢贸易，统治者接受摩尼教。840年被黠戛斯击败后，回鹘人南迁塔里木绿洲。
zh.significance: 回鹘是较早建城并接受世界性宗教的草原帝国，其后继者又向蒙古人传播文字。

title: Abbasid Caliphate
summary: The Abbasids overthrew the Umayyads and moved the capital to Baghdad, which became one of the largest cities in the world. Their caliphs lost real power to regional dynasties from the 9th century on, but remained the symbolic heads of Sunni Islam until the Mongols took Baghdad in 1258.
significance: Abbasid Baghdad was the center of a flowering of science, medicine, mathematics and philosophy that preserved and extended Greek, Persian and Indian learning.

zh.title: 阿拔斯王朝
zh.summary: 阿拔斯推翻倭马亚，将首都迁往巴格达，后者发展为世界最大城市之一。自9世纪起，地方王朝逐步夺走实权，但哈里发仍为逊尼派伊斯兰教的象征领袖，直到1258年蒙古攻陷巴格达。
zh.significance: 阿拔斯时期的巴格达是科学、医学、数学与哲学中心，保存并发展了希腊、波斯与印度知识。

title: Abbasid Caliphate founded

location.name: Kufa (where the first Abbasid caliph was proclaimed)

summary: A revolt that began in Khorasan, in eastern Iran, defeats the last Umayyad caliph at the Battle of the Zab in northern Iraq. Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah, a descendant of Muhammad's uncle Abbas, had already been proclaimed caliph at Kufa, and now founds the Abbasid dynasty. Many members of the Umayyad family are massacred, though one, Abd al-Rahman, escapes to Spain.
significance: The Abbasids moved the center of the Islamic world east to Iraq, and under later caliphs their capital Baghdad became the heart of a golden age of trade, science and scholarship.

zh.title: 阿拔斯王朝建立
zh.summary: 呼罗珊起义军在伊拉克北部扎卜河战役击败最后一位倭马亚哈里发。穆罕默德叔父阿拔斯的后裔阿布·阿拔斯·萨法赫此前已在库法称哈里发，由此建立阿拔斯王朝。许多倭马亚家族成员被杀，阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼等人逃往西班牙。
zh.significance: 阿拔斯将伊斯兰世界重心东移至伊拉克，后来以巴格达为中心，开启贸易、科学与学术的黄金时代。
zh.locationName: 库法（首位阿拔斯哈里发即位地）

title: Abbasid translation movement
summary: Patrons and multilingual scholars translate Greek philosophy, medicine and mathematics into Arabic, often through Syriac. Baghdad becomes a major center of this work during the eighth to tenth centuries.
significance: Translation preserved and transformed earlier learning, providing material for new research in the Islamic world and later in Europe.

zh.title: 阿拔斯翻译运动
zh.summary: 赞助者与多语学者将希腊哲学、医学和数学译成阿拉伯语，常以叙利亚语译本为中介。8至10世纪，巴格达成为这项工作的主要中心。
zh.significance: 翻译保存并改造了早期知识，为伊斯兰世界及后来欧洲的新研究提供材料。

title: Islamic Golden Age (approx.)
summary: Scholars across the Islamic world advanced mathematics, medicine, astronomy, philosophy, and literature, drawing on and extending earlier traditions. This band uses the Abbasid-era convention; cultural activity extended beyond these dates and across several regions.
significance: Its scholars preserved and extended ancient learning and made original advances, such as algebra and clinical medicine, that later passed to Europe.

zh.title: 伊斯兰黄金时代（约）
zh.summary: 伊斯兰世界的学者继承并发展先前传统，在数学、医学、天文、哲学和文学方面取得重要进展。此处采用常见的阿拔斯时代划分，但文化活动跨越这些年代，也分布于多个地区。
zh.significance: 学者保存古代知识，并在代数与临床医学等领域取得原创进展，后来又将这些成果传入欧洲。
zh.dateLabel: 约公元750年-1258年；起止年代说法不一

title: Golden age of Tang poetry
summary: In the middle of the 8th century, Li Bai and Du Fu, later judged the two greatest poets in the Chinese language, are both writing, alongside Wang Wei and many others. Skill in verse is tested in the civil service examinations and expected of every educated person; some 49,000 poems from the Tang survive.
significance: Tang poems have been memorized by Chinese schoolchildren ever since and set the standard for poetry across East Asia.

zh.title: 唐诗的黄金时代
zh.summary: 8世纪中叶，李白、杜甫与王维等诗人活跃，他们后来被视为中国诗歌的代表人物。诗赋能力是科举考查和士人修养的一部分，现存唐诗约四万九千首。
zh.significance: 唐诗此后一直被中国学生诵读，并为整个东亚的诗歌创作树立典范。

title: Battle of Talas
summary: An Abbasid army defeats Tang Chinese forces near the Talas River, in today's Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, reportedly after the Tang army's Karluk Turk allies change sides. A famous story says Chinese prisoners taken here taught papermaking in Samarkand, but historians think paper had probably reached Central Asia earlier.
significance: It marked the westernmost reach of Tang China, which soon lost its hold on Central Asia during the An Lushan Rebellion, leaving the region open to Islamic and Turkic influence.

zh.title: 怛罗斯之战
zh.summary: 阿拔斯军在怛罗斯河附近击败唐军，据记载唐的葛逻禄盟军临阵倒戈。中国俘虏将造纸传至撒马尔罕的故事广为流传，但纸可能更早已到中亚。
zh.significance: 此役标志唐朝西进的界限；安史之乱后，唐更失去中亚控制，该地区逐渐转向伊斯兰与突厥文化。

title: Bulguksa and Seokguram built
summary: Kim Daeseong, chief minister of Silla, begins the temple of Bulguksa and, on the mountain above it, the Seokguram grotto, a domed chamber of fitted granite blocks around a seated Buddha who faces the sunrise over the East Sea.
significance: The two are the masterpieces of Buddhist art and architecture from Silla and remain among Korea's most treasured monuments.

zh.title: 佛国寺与石窟庵建造
zh.summary: 新罗大臣金大城主持修建佛国寺及山上的石窟庵。石窟庵以精密拼合的花岗岩构成穹顶石室，中央坐佛面向东方海上的日出。
zh.significance: 二者是新罗佛教艺术与建筑的杰作，也是朝鲜半岛最珍贵的古迹之一。

title: Great Buddha of Todai-ji dedicated
summary: Emperor Shomu, hoping to protect Japan from epidemics and unrest, has a bronze Buddha about 15 meters high cast at the temple of Todai-ji in Nara, using much of the country's copper. An Indian monk paints in the statue's eyes at a ceremony attended by thousands of monks and envoys from abroad.
significance: The project made Buddhism a religion of the Japanese state; the hall that houses the statue is still one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.

zh.title: 东大寺大佛开光
zh.summary: 圣武天皇希望借佛教消除疫病与动乱，在奈良东大寺铸造约15米高的铜佛，耗用全国大量铜料。开光仪式由印度僧人为佛像点睛，数千僧人与外国使节参加。
zh.significance: 工程强化了佛教作为国家宗教的地位，安放佛像的大殿至今仍是世界最大的木构建筑之一。

title: An Lushan Rebellion

location.name: Fanyang, near present-day Beijing (An Lushan's base)

summary: An Lushan, a powerful Tang general of Sogdian and Turkic descent, rebels from his base in the northeast and captures both Tang capitals, Luoyang and Chang'an. The war lasts until 763. Census figures fall dramatically, but historians think this partly reflects the collapse of record-keeping as well as mass deaths.
significance: The Tang survived, but much weakened: regional governors gained lasting power, and China lost control of Central Asia.

zh.title: 安史之乱
zh.summary: 具有粟特与突厥血统的唐朝将领安禄山从东北根据地起兵，攻占洛阳与长安。战争持续至763年。户籍数字骤减，但历史学家认为，这不仅反映大量死亡，也部分源于登记制度崩溃。
zh.significance: 唐朝虽得以延续，却严重衰弱：地方节度使获得持久权力，唐也失去了对中亚的控制。
zh.locationName: 范阳，今北京附近（安禄山的根据地）

title: Al-Andalus (Umayyad Córdoba)
summary: A prince of the Umayyad family who escaped the Abbasid takeover founded an independent emirate at Córdoba in 756, and in 929 his descendant took the title of caliph. Under them Córdoba became one of the largest cities in Europe, known for its great mosque, libraries and scholars. The caliphate broke up into small rival kingdoms after 1031.
significance: Muslim Spain passed Arabic science, philosophy and much of the learning of ancient Greece on to Latin Europe.

zh.title: 安达卢斯（科尔多瓦倭马亚政权）
zh.summary: 逃离阿拔斯追杀的倭马亚王子于756年在科尔多瓦建立独立政权，后裔于929年称哈里发。科尔多瓦以大清真寺、图书馆和学者闻名，1031年后分裂为诸小国。
zh.significance: 穆斯林西班牙向拉丁欧洲传播阿拉伯科学、哲学与大量古希腊知识。

title: Papal States
summary: The Frankish king Pippin gave the pope the lands around Rome and Ravenna in 756, and for eleven centuries the popes ruled a band of central Italy as princes as well as heads of the Church. The Kingdom of Italy took most of it in 1860 and Rome itself in 1870.
significance: Their own territory made the popes a political power in Europe, and its loss left the question of the pope's status open until the creation of Vatican City in 1929.

zh.title: 教皇国
zh.summary: 法兰克王丕平于756年将罗马、拉文纳附近领土交给教皇。此后约十一世纪，教皇既是宗教领袖，也治理意大利中部领地。意大利于1860年夺取大部，1870年占领罗马。
zh.significance: 世俗领地使教皇成为欧洲政治强权；领土丧失后的地位争议，直到1929年梵蒂冈城建立才获解决。

title: Baghdad founded
summary: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founds a new capital on the Tigris River, close to where it nears the Euphrates, built as a great round city with the caliph's palace and mosque at its center. Its location on river and caravan routes draws merchants from across Asia.
significance: Baghdad grew into one of the largest and richest cities in the world and a center of scholarship where Greek, Persian and Indian learning was translated into Arabic.

zh.title: 巴格达建城
zh.summary: 阿拔斯哈里发曼苏尔在底格里斯河畔、靠近幼发拉底河处营建新都，设计为以宫殿和清真寺为中心的大型圆城。河流与陆路交通吸引了亚洲各地商人。
zh.significance: 巴格达成为世界最大、最富有的城市之一，也是将希腊、波斯和印度学术译成阿拉伯文的重要中心。

title: Tang introduces the Two-Tax system
summary: The Tang government introduces a new fiscal system associated with minister Yang Yan, collecting taxes in summer and autumn with greater attention to property and resources.
significance: The reform marked a shift away from earlier household and labor obligations toward a different basis for imperial revenue.

zh.title: 唐朝实行两税法
zh.summary: 唐朝政府在杨炎推动下实行新财政制度，于夏秋两季征税，更重视财产与经济资源。
zh.significance: 改革标志着帝国财政逐步摆脱早期以户籍和劳役为核心的负担体系。

title: Viking raid on Lindisfarne
summary: Raiders from Scandinavia attack the monastery on the island of Lindisfarne, off the coast of Northumbria in northeastern England, killing monks and carrying off treasures and captives. The scholar Alcuin writes that such terror had never before appeared in Britain.
significance: The raid is traditionally seen as the start of the Viking Age, when Norse raiders, traders and settlers reached from North America to the Caspian Sea.

zh.title: 维京人袭击林迪斯法恩
zh.summary: 斯堪的纳维亚袭击者洗劫英格兰东北海岸林迪斯法恩修道院，杀害僧侣，带走财宝和俘虏，引发当时学者震惊。
zh.significance: 此事通常被视为维京时代开端，随后北欧袭击者、商人与定居者的足迹远达北美和里海。

title: Viking Age
summary: Seafarers from Scandinavia raided, traded, and settled from the North Atlantic to the rivers of eastern Europe, founding communities in the British Isles, Normandy, Iceland, and Greenland. The band runs from the raid on Lindisfarne to the Norman conquest of England, the conventional dates in English-language histories.
significance: The Vikings redrew the map of northern Europe, founding or reshaping states from Russia to Normandy and England, and were the first Europeans to reach North America.

zh.title: 维京时代
zh.summary: 斯堪的纳维亚航海者在北大西洋与东欧河道贸易、劫掠和定居，在不列颠、诺曼底、冰岛和格陵兰建立社群。此处采用793年至1066年的常见划分。
zh.significance: 维京人重塑北欧政治版图，也是最早抵达北美的欧洲人。
zh.dateLabel: 公元793年-1066年；惯用年代范围

title: Heian Japan
summary: With the capital at Heian-kyo, modern Kyoto, the Japanese imperial court reached its cultural height under the dominance of the Fujiwara family. Court ladies wrote classics such as The Tale of Genji, while real power in the provinces passed to warrior clans.
significance: The period shaped a distinctly Japanese literature, script and aesthetic, and its end marked the rise of the samurai who would rule Japan for seven centuries.

zh.title: 日本平安时期
zh.summary: 日本朝廷以平安京、今京都为中心，在藤原氏主导下达到宫廷文化高峰。宫廷女性写出《源氏物语》等经典，地方实权却逐渐转入武士家族之手。
zh.significance: 这一时期形成了独特的日本文学、文字与审美，其结束也标志着此后七百年武士统治的兴起。

title: Book of Kells illuminated
summary: Monastic artists produce an elaborately decorated Latin Gospel manuscript around AD 800. Its precise place of production is debated, with Iona and Kells closely associated with its history.
significance: The manuscript is a celebrated example of Insular art, combining intricate ornament with the transmission of Christian scripture.

zh.title: 《凯尔经》绘成
zh.summary: 修道院艺术家约于公元800年制作华丽装饰的拉丁文福音书抄本。确切制作地点仍有争议，爱奥那与凯尔斯均与其历史密切相关。
zh.significance: 它是岛屿艺术的著名范例，将精密装饰与基督教经典的传承结合起来。
zh.locationName: 苏格兰爱奥那岛（传统关联地点）

title: Borobudur built
summary: In central Java, rulers of the Sailendra dynasty build Borobudur, a vast Buddhist monument shaped as a stepped mountain topped by stupas. Pilgrims walking up its terraces pass more than 2,600 carved relief panels and over 500 statues of the Buddha. Construction probably takes several decades.
significance: Often described as the largest Buddhist monument in the world, Borobudur shows how deeply Indian religion and art had taken root in island Southeast Asia.

zh.title: 婆罗浮屠建造
zh.summary: 爪哇中部夏连特拉王朝修建婆罗浮屠，形如层层上升、顶有佛塔的巨型山丘。朝圣者沿台地绕行，可见两千六百余幅浮雕和五百余尊佛像。建设可能持续数十年。
zh.significance: 婆罗浮屠常被称为世界最大的佛教建筑遗迹，见证印度宗教与艺术在东南亚群岛的深厚影响。

title: Carolingian Empire
summary: Charlemagne, king of the Franks, united most of western and central Europe and was crowned emperor in Rome in 800. His court promoted learning and church reform, but his grandsons divided the empire in 843 and it had dissolved by 888.
significance: It revived the idea of empire in the West and its division produced the kingdoms that became France and Germany.

zh.title: 加洛林帝国
zh.summary: 查理曼统一西欧和中欧大部，800年加冕为帝，宫廷推动教育与教会改革。其孙辈于843年分割帝国，至888年整体瓦解。
zh.significance: 它复兴了西欧帝国观念，分裂后形成的王国成为法国和德国的前身。

title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
summary: On Christmas Day, Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne, king of the Franks and Lombards, as emperor in Rome. Charlemagne already rules much of western and central Europe, from the Pyrenees to the Elbe.
significance: It revived the title of emperor in the West for the first time since 476 and tied together the papacy, the Frankish monarchy and the Roman imperial idea, laying foundations for medieval Europe and the later Holy Roman Empire.

zh.title: 查理曼加冕称帝
zh.summary: 圣诞节，教皇利奥三世在罗马为法兰克与伦巴第国王查理曼加冕。此时其疆域已覆盖从比利牛斯山至易北河的广大地区。
zh.significance: 西方自476年后首次恢复皇帝称号，将教皇、法兰克王权与罗马帝国传统连接，影响后来的神圣罗马帝国。

title: Swahili trading cities flourish
summary: Independent African port cities grow along the East African coast, linking inland producers with Indian Ocean merchants. Their Swahili-speaking societies develop distinctive urban, Islamic and maritime traditions; these dates show an approximate phase of growth.
significance: The cities made East Africa a major participant in trade and cultural exchange across the Indian Ocean.

zh.title: 斯瓦希里贸易城市繁荣
zh.summary: 独立的非洲港口城市沿东非海岸发展，将内陆生产者与印度洋商人相连接。斯瓦希里语社会形成独特的城市、伊斯兰与海洋传统；这些年代标示一个大致发展阶段。
zh.significance: 这些城市使东非成为印度洋贸易与文化交流的重要参与者。

title: Khmer Empire
summary: From their capital at Angkor in Cambodia, the Khmer kings ruled much of mainland Southeast Asia. They built vast reservoirs and canals and hundreds of stone temples, including Angkor Wat and the Bayon, first for Hindu gods and later for the Buddha.
significance: Angkor was among the largest cities of the pre-industrial world, and its temples remain the national symbol of Cambodia.

zh.title: 高棉帝国
zh.summary: 高棉诸王以吴哥为中心统治东南亚大陆大部，修建巨大水库、运河和吴哥窟、巴戎寺等石构神庙，信仰从印度教逐步转向佛教。
zh.significance: 吴哥是前工业时代世界最大的城市区域之一，其神庙至今仍是柬埔寨的国家象征。

title: Al-Khwarizmi and algebra
summary: In Baghdad, the Persian scholar Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi writes a book on solving equations by 'completion and balancing', in Arabic al-jabr. He also writes on the Indian system of numerals, including zero, a work known mainly from later Latin translations.
significance: The word 'algebra' comes from his book's title and 'algorithm' from his name, and Latin translations of his works helped bring algebra and Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe.

zh.title: 花拉子米与代数学
zh.summary: 波斯学者花拉子米在巴格达著书，以“还原与对消”方法求解方程。他还介绍包含零在内的印度数制，该部分著作主要通过后世拉丁文译本传世。
zh.significance: “代数”一词源于其书名，“算法”的欧洲语言名称源于其姓名。拉丁译本推动代数与印度-阿拉伯数字在欧洲传播。

title: Treaty of Verdun divides the Carolingian realm
summary: Charlemagne's grandsons divide the empire into western, middle and eastern kingdoms after civil war. The agreement settles an immediate dynastic conflict, not modern national boundaries.
significance: The division became a major turning point in the political development of western and central Europe.

zh.title: 《凡尔登条约》分割加洛林帝国
zh.summary: 内战后，查理曼的孙辈将帝国分为西部、中部与东部王国。协议解决的是当时的王朝冲突，而非划定现代国家边界。
zh.significance: 这一分割成为西欧与中欧政治发展的重要转折。

title: Tang court suppresses Buddhist monasteries
summary: Emperor Wuzong orders the closure of many Buddhist monasteries and the return of monks and nuns to lay life. Confiscation of property forms part of a wider campaign against religious institutions.
significance: The campaign sharply reduced institutional Buddhism and exposed tensions between monastic wealth and state power.

zh.title: 唐武宗会昌灭佛
zh.summary: 唐武宗下令关闭大量佛寺，勒令僧尼还俗，并没收财产，构成针对宗教机构的广泛打击。
zh.significance: 运动严重削弱了制度化佛教，凸显寺院财富与国家权力之间的矛盾。

title: Chola Empire
summary: The Chola kings of the Tamil country conquered southern India and Sri Lanka, and under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I sent fleets across the Bay of Bengal as far as Srivijaya. They built great temples such as the Brihadisvara at Thanjavur and commissioned fine bronze sculpture.
significance: The Cholas were one of the few Indian powers to project force overseas, and they carried Tamil trade and culture to Southeast Asia.

zh.title: 朱罗王朝
zh.summary: 泰米尔朱罗王朝征服南印度和斯里兰卡，在罗阇罗阇一世、拉金德拉一世时期派舰队远征室利佛逝，营建坦贾武尔大寺并制作精美铜像。
zh.significance: 朱罗是少数能跨海投射军力的印度政权，将泰米尔贸易与文化传播到东南亚。

title: Pagan Kingdom
summary: From the city of Pagan on the Irrawaddy, King Anawrahta united the valley in the 11th century, the first state to rule most of what is now Myanmar. Its kings and people adopted Theravada Buddhism and built more than ten thousand temples on the plain around the capital. The kingdom collapsed after Mongol invasions in the 1280s.
significance: Pagan established the Burmese language, script and Theravada Buddhism as the basis of Burmese culture.

zh.title: 蒲甘王国
zh.summary: 11世纪，阿奴律陀以伊洛瓦底河畔的蒲甘为中心统一河谷，建立首个统治今缅甸大部的国家。君民接受上座部佛教，在首都周围修建万余寺塔。13世纪80年代蒙古入侵后，王国瓦解。
zh.significance: 蒲甘使缅语、缅文与上座部佛教成为缅甸文化的基础。

title: Chaco Canyon great houses
